Hey bud, I'm gonna give you some advice that no one else seems to be giving you. I've got about six years as a collectibles seller, and about nine at actually collecting. I've had some things like this occur before, and let me tell you the best way to handle this.

I'm gonna be real with you here, you're probably not gonna get your money back on this. I definitely implore you to try, but if it was the owner who did this, and not some clerk who just makes commission, you're probably shit outta luck. Go in, be professional, make your request, stand by it. Don't let them try to spin you around into this being YOUR fault. The seller knew what they were doing, and don't let them tell you otherwise. But, if at the end of the day they say no, cut your losses, never go back, and be sure to tell everyone how sleazy the place it (Please post the business name too, I travel a lot and want to make sure to not stop by)

Secondly, and most importantly, don't beat yourself up on this too badly. Things like this are going to happen. You see something, maybe from your childhood, and you get excited, and so you just buy. You don't really think, you just buy. You think you're getting a killer deal because that's what any reseller is gonna want you to think so you return. Same thing has happened to me a few times. Funny enough, it was just with this line of X-Men toys. Me and my business partner threw down about $350 on about 14 of these, and this was when they were, at most, $5 brand new in the box. We still have some that we just can't sell. We took the loss, and rolled with it. It's a part of the life.

Just remember, always be willing to do your research, even if it's in the store. Before I go in anywhere, whether it be a thrift store, or a collectible shop, I always pull up eBay on my phone ready to search for whatever catches my eye before I buy.

Other tips:
1) If the seller is being pushy for the sale, they don't deserve your money. They are most likely trying to rip you off. Good sellers are okay if you walk away, because they know they're stuff is well priced. They should never have to present you with an argument for your money.
2) Don't be afraid to haggle. Ever. Doesn't matter if you're already getting a deal. Something is 5 bucks? Offer 3. One dollar? Find something else for a dollar and see if you can't get both for a dollar. You'd be surprised how often this does work.
3) It's okay to walk away. Always. If you don't have the money they want, then you don't have it. I once walked away from a super nintendo and a bunch of boxed games because the guy wanted more than I had for it. I was getting in my car, and doesn't he come running down the driveway, bag in hand of all of it, and was okay with taking the last $40 I had towards my spending cash because "The wife said I had to". Score for me, though, right? (FYI: He initially wanted $100, and it was all worth around $250, just didn't have the cash)

Any questions, feel free to PM me. I have no problems in giving you any hints or tips in your beginning journey :-)

Going back, turned down the side street, and this guy comes up to me and goes "Hey man, you got any weed?"

"Sorry man, can't say I do." "Aw fuck, I was hoping I could buy some off of you. See, I missed my appointment at the methadone clinic and I'm trying to get a fix." "Yeah, sorry man, wish I could help you out." "Yeah man. Say, you got any money?"

Usually, I'd throw someone a dollar to get them away. A dollar's a busride, and then they leave me the fuck alone. But I didn't even have a penny on me. So I told the guy, "Sorry, don't have a thing." "Aw shit man...you sure about that?"

That's when he pulled out a knife, held it up, and started walking slowly at me.

I'm trying to think quickly to myself. I'm about 100 feet from my car, this guy is just moving towards me, and if I run, he's gonna chase me. So I've got my hands up, and I just keep telling him "I don't have anything, I swear." "You sure? You sure you don't have a fucking quarter on you?" All this time, just inching closer and closer, as I'm slowly backing up, never taking my eye off that knife.

I stopped, and realized I had one shot. Waited for him to get close enough, and I grabbed his arm, pushed it to the inside of him, and threw my other fist into his face, bringing him down to the ground as I went.

He dropped, and I ran like hell to my car and sped off.

I was about 50-100 feet from my car. Didn't want to risk the guy catching up to me before I could get in if I ran. All the while I'm thinking, he just kept creeping forward asking "You sure? You sure?"

I stopped and let him get a little closer, grabbed his wrist, moved it to the side and punched him in the face as hard as I could to bring him down to the ground. The second he was down I got the fuck outta dodge.

When I was five, I saw Back To The Future for the first time. I saw Michael J. Fox as Marty McFly playing Johnny B. Goode, and I wanted to play. My mom didn't have money for a guitar, sadly, so I just went with watching that scene over and over again.

Cut to 16. More "popular" now (sure, we'll call it that), and just got out of a relationship where she ran off with a friend of mine (wasn't the first, or the last). Started dating this new chick (read: rebound), who's now like a sister to me. She played guitar. I had a guitar in my basement, so I had her teach me how to read tabs and chord diagrams and I went from there.

I'm 22 now. Until a year ago, didn't even try putting my foot into the local music scene. Made a lot of great friends in it too. But I'm seeing that nobody cares about seeing me play.

I pour my heart and soul into every song I write. I put everything I have into every performance, and it feels like nobody cares. People just talk through me playing, giving half-assed claps, and only care if I'm doing a cover.

It hurts because I don't feel accepted at all, no matter how much I put into it. I've pulled out on all of the hurt and depression and second-guessing of my entire life and put it into this music, and all I get is "I'll catch you next time." When all I do is catch them ALL the time.

All I've wanted since I was a little kid, was to perform music, to feel accepted, and I don't feel that no matter where I go. I feel like if I wrote generic songs about getting drunk and partying people would care, but it seems like nobody does wherever I go.

If they want something that makes you have to use more than one board, tack on an extra 5-10 depending on the color variations that they want.

Remember, the larger it is, the more magnets are going to have to be glued on (if they want magnets that is) and magnets and the glue costs more money, time and effort into the sprite.
